newsitem.title: BELGIUM: CREDIT LYONNAIS BELGIUM TO OFFER FREE BANK ACCOUNTS.
newsitem.headline: CREDIT LYONNAIS BELGIUM TO OFFER FREE BANK ACCOUNTS.

text.p: Credit Lyonnais Belgium, a unit of France's Credit Lyonnais, said on Tuesday it would offer free current accounts to customers from February.
"As of February we will have accounts for current transactions which will be totally free of charge," said Yves Delacollette, the bank's director of retail operations, told a news conference.
Delacollette estimated that Belgium's leading banks charge their customers on average about 3,000 Belgian francs a year in transaction and management costs.
Delacollette said CLB would also send bank statements to its customers free of charge, once a week.
The sole condition for a free bank account is that customers have at least 500,000 Belgian francs of savings or investments with CLB.
The bank has 220,000 customers who have, on average, one million francs of savings or investments deposited at the bank.
Delacollette said CLB hoped to open about 10,000 free bank accounts this year. "In theory we could have a much higher number but the inertia on current accounts is very high," he said.
